items.question: Which columns appear in the CSV, in what order, and with what header text?
items.ticket: download their requisition list (with status and fill counts) as CSV
items.chose: Emits the header "Requisition ID,Title,Status,Openings,Filled,Created" with six columns: id, title, status, openings, filled, created.
items.instead: Use snake_case or lowercase headers, or leave out the created date or the title.

items.question: What order are the rows in?
items.chose: Sorts a copy of the input by creation time ascending, then by id compared by code unit.
items.instead: Keep the caller's input order, or sort newest first.

items.question: Does the builder reorder the caller's array?
items.chose: Sorts a shallow copy, so the input array is left unchanged.
items.instead: Sort the input array in place.

items.question: Which line terminator ends each row, and does the last row have one?
items.chose: Ends every row, including the header and the last row, with \r\n.
items.instead: Use \n, and leave off the trailing newline.

items.question: Does the output start with a UTF-8 BOM?
items.chose: Prepends a BOM character (U+FEFF) to the output.
items.instead: Emit no BOM, so the output is plain CSV text.

items.question: What does an empty requisition list produce?
items.chose: Returns the BOM and the header row only.
items.instead: Return an empty string, or throw.

items.question: How is a missing or null title written?
items.chose: Writes an empty field for a null or undefined title.
items.instead: Write a placeholder such as "(untitled)", or the text "null".

items.question: How are fields containing commas, quotes or line breaks escaped?
items.chose: Wraps the field in double quotes and doubles any inner quotes when it contains a comma, quote, CR or LF.
items.instead: Quote every field, or also neutralise leading =, +, - or @ against spreadsheet formula injection.

items.question: How is the creation time formatted?
items.chose: Writes the time as a UTC ISO 8601 string with milliseconds, using toISOString().
items.instead: Write a date only (YYYY-MM-DD), or a locale or local-time format.

items.question: Are rows with bad data (unknown status, bad counts, invalid date) skipped, repaired or rejected?
items.chose: Validates every row before building anything, and throws an Error naming the requisition id on the first bad row. Bad data means a status outside open/on_hold/filled/cancelled, openings or filled that is not a whole number of at least 0, filled greater than openings, or an invalid createdAt.
items.instead: Skip the bad rows, or write them as they are and flag them.

items.question: Which status values are allowed, and are they written raw or relabelled?
items.chose: Accepts only open, on_hold, filled and cancelled, and writes the raw value without relabelling it.
items.instead: Pass any status string through, or write human-readable labels such as "On hold".

items.question: Are duplicate requisition ids accepted?
items.chose: Does not check for duplicates. Every duplicate row is written, in sorted order.
items.instead: Reject duplicates with an error, or drop them.
